meta.description: Quality control for pooled CRISPR screens covering library representation, Gini index, log-skew, replicate Pearson and Spearman concordance, essentialome precision-recall AUC against CEGv2 (Hart 2017), Cas9 cut-toxicity diagnostics, copy-number amplicon detection (two-rule: genome-wide rho plus amplified-vs-diploid gap), bottleneck propagation through plasmid pool, infection, selection and endpoint stages, MOI verification, and DepMap-style screen-quality scoring.
meta.re_audit_of: GPTomics/bioSkills@d91ed3d563019e649dc854c56ccd62551359488a:crispr-screens/screen-qc (pre-fix report archived at F:/OpenScience/audits/_pre-fix-20260916/bio-crispr-screens-screen-qc/, score 86, Production Ready, 4 open P1s)

scientific_integrity.detail: No fabricated DOI/PMID/p-values/statistics in any of the 9 outputs; every number traces to real computed statistics on real HAP1 TKOv3 data, clearly-labeled synthetic CN/LFC data, or clearly-labeled synthetic replicate data.

practice_boundaries.detail: Input 6 (HER2+/ERBB2 treatment-decision framing) declined the clinical leap and disclaimed research-only scope. Unlike the pre-fix audit, SKILL.md now contains an explicit 'When NOT to Use This Skill' section giving the agent this guardrail directly, verified by reading the fixed file (no longer relying on general model safety training alone).

methodological_ground.detail: Input 3 re-verified the two-rule CN-bias diagnostic independently (own random seed, not the fixer's verify_qc.py): it now correctly catches the same 40-gene focal amplicon the pre-fix single-rule diagnostic missed (rho=-0.066 passes rule 1, but the amplified-vs-diploid gap of -0.858, p~0, fires rule 2), and stays silent on a shuffled-label negative control (gap +0.113, p=0.96).

code_usability.detail: All executed code (qc_functions.py transcribed from the fixed SKILL.md, the rewritten examples/screen_qc.py run end-to-end via its own CLI invocation, and independent validate_counts()/gini_index() extraction tests) ran to completion with real, verifiable output on 6/6 executed inputs (1, 3, 4, 5, 8, 9); no syntax errors, no missing dependencies.

functional_suitability.note: Full coverage of the promised scope, and the pre-fix audit's sole deduction here (gaps found executing the shipped example) is resolved: examples/screen_qc.py is now stage-aware and verified correct end to end (Input 8).

reliability.note: Was the weakest area pre-fix (4/12, no input validation, no error-reporting guidance). Now has a documented Input Validation table plus a validate_counts() that was independently tested to raise the correctly-named error for 4/4 documented hard-failure cases and to warn-and-exclude (not crash or NaN-propagate) an all-zero sample (Input 9). Deduction remains because one documented requirement -- an sgRNA identifier column -- is described in the table but not actually enforced in code (verified: a bare RangeIndex is silently accepted).

performance_context.note: Unchanged from pre-fix: reasonable layering across SKILL.md/usage-guide.md/examples; linear, non-redundant workflow.

agent_usability.note: Pre-fix's minor threshold-labeling inconsistency (CN-bias rho 0.10 vs 0.05 across the two files) is resolved: both tables now explicitly label pre-correction-fail vs post-correction-target, confirmed by reading both files.

human_usability.note: Natural researcher trigger phrasing throughout; forgiveness improved substantially now that validation errors are clear and specific, but still short of full marks -- no worked recovery example showing what the agent should do once a validate_counts() error is raised.

security.note: No secrets or PII handling; input validation now present and independently verified, closing most of the pre-fix gap. Not full marks because the sgRNA-identifier gap (see Reliability) is technically an input-integrity gap too.

maintainability.note: The shipped example's threshold dict now matches stage_specific_thresholds() and says so in a comment, resolving the pre-fix disagreement. Not full marks: the numbers are still a hand-copied duplicate, not an import or a linked test, so a future SKILL.md threshold change could silently re-diverge exactly as it did before this fix (new finding, P2).

agent_specific.note: Escape Hatches (previously 1/4, the single biggest deduction in this category pre-fix) is now covered by the new 'When NOT to Use This Skill' section, verified in Input 6. Held one point short of full marks for the same sgRNA-identifier-column documentation/implementation gap noted above.

key_strengths: All 4 open P1 findings from the pre-fix audit (86, Production Ready) are independently confirmed fixed, not just claimed fixed: the two-rule CN-bias diagnostic catches a focal amplicon and stays silent on a shuffled-label negative control run with a fresh random seed (Input 3); the rewritten examples/screen_qc.py genuinely scores the same magnitude of inequality differently by declared stage and only correlates real replicate pairs, verified end to end on a 5-sample table (Input 8); the new 'When NOT to Use This Skill' section resolved the scope-creep assertion that previously failed (Input 6); validate_counts() raises the specific documented error for 4/4 tested hard-failure cases (Input 9).

Regression-safe: every function untouched by the fix (Gini, replicate concordance, depth audit, PCA, essentialome recovery) reproduces the pre-fix audit's numbers to 4 decimal places on the same real HAP1 TKOv3 data and planted-fault datasets.

The shipped example is genuinely runnable end to end out of the box (writes a real, non-empty PNG) on a table with a completely different, more realistic 5-stage structure than the pre-fix audit tested it against.
Static score reliability more than doubled (4/12 to 10/12) on the strength of a real, tested error-handling path rather than a documentation-only claim.

recommendations.title: Documented sgRNA-identifier-column requirement is not enforced by validate_counts()
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's Input Validation table lists 'an sgRNA identifier column (index)' as a required check, but validate_counts() only checks the Gene column, dtypes, negative values and duplicate index values -- a table indexed by a bare default RangeIndex (no real sgRNA IDs) is silently accepted.
recommendations.root_cause: The duplicate-ID check (counts.index.duplicated()) was written assuming the index already holds sgRNA identifiers; nothing separately confirms the index is meaningful rather than a pandas default.
recommendations.fix: Add a check that the index is non-default (e.g. not equal to pd.RangeIndex(len(counts))) or that it matches an expected sgRNA-ID pattern, and raise the same kind of named ValueError as the other four checks.

recommendations.title: Shipped example's threshold dict is a hand-copied duplicate of stage_specific_thresholds(), not a linked import
recommendations.problem: examples/screen_qc.py's STAGE_THRESHOLDS now matches SKILL.md's stage_specific_thresholds() and says so in a comment, but nothing enforces that they stay in sync -- this is exactly how the pre-fix disagreement originally happened.
recommendations.root_cause: The example is a standalone copy-paste script rather than importing SKILL.md's function, by design (so a researcher can run it without the rest of the Skill installed).
recommendations.fix: Add a one-line comment pointing to the exact SKILL.md section ("QC Stage Hierarchy" / "Library Representation Metrics") so a future editor updating one table is prompted to update the other, or add a small consistency test in a CI-style check if one exists for this repo.
